# Reflection on the MSc Project

### Project Summary

My MSc project evaluated the feasibility of using locally hosted Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to computationally integrate and analyse both qualitative and quantitative clinical trial data. Using a dataset from the LQD trial for treatment-resistant depression, I designed and applied three mixed-method analytical tasks: Convergence, Explanatory, and Statistical. Because a human expert baseline was unavailable, I developed an automated "LLM-as-a-Judge" evaluation strategy using custom scoring rubrics to assess the model's output. The project successfully demonstrated that MLLMs exhibit strong logical reasoning and factual consistency when triangulating clinical data, providing a foundational framework for future computational clinical analysis.

### Skills Developed

Throughout the research process, I developed advanced technical data analysis and project management skills, specifically by deploying and configuring language models on a High-Performance Cluster (CREATE). I also significantly enhanced my critical thinking and problem-solving abilities by designing multi-stage "chain-of-thought" prompting pipelines and systematically evaluating the complex logical relationships generated by the AI.

### Challenges and Solutions

|  |  |
|----|----|
| **Challenge** | **How I Overcame It** |
| **Out-Of-Memory (OOM) Errors:** Limited computing resources on the HPC caused frequent memory crashes during analysis. | I implemented model quantization to load weights in 4-bit precision, utilized memory-efficient scaled dot-product attention, and divided massive qualitative transcripts into smaller, memory-safe batches. |
| **Clinical Misinterpretation:** The model incorrectly assumed a lower QIDS-SR score indicated more severe depression symptoms. | I refined the prompt engineering by adding targeted system prompts that explicitly provided the correct clinical context and scale interpretation. |
| **Data Pipeline Failures:** The LLM-generated Python code failed to locate specific data columns in the unseen quantitative dataset. | I updated the prompt instructions to include a detailed glossary of variable names, ensuring the model had the necessary context to generate functional code. |
